findings.claim: The skill orders the agent to run `adversarial-review` and `sycophancy-correction` but neither is bundled, pathed, or given any invocation syntax, so the step cannot be followed as written.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md line 33-34: "run `adversarial-review` once and screen its findings with `sycophancy-correction`"; script_inventory lists only `scripts/kbd-bottleneck-detector.sh` and file_tree contains no other executable or reference defining these commands.
findings.suggested_fix: State the resolved path or command for each tool (e.g. a repo-relative binary or sibling skill), and define the expected input/output of the screening step.

findings.claim: The skill expands adversarial review beyond the terminal-only triggers the intent specified, adding mid-lifecycle triggers the intent never asked for.
findings.evidence: original_intent: "terminal-only adversarial review with sycophancy screening"; SKILL.md lines 31-33: "At phase or child completion, on ambiguous canonical authority, or after the same violation twice at one revision, run `adversarial-review` once" — the second and third triggers are not terminal events.
findings.suggested_fix: Either restrict review to phase/child completion per the intent, or get the intent updated to sanction the additional triggers.

findings.claim: "An unavailable or unresolved review blocks certification" contradicts the repo constraint that a missing screening binary degrades gracefully (log skip and pass), leaving the agent with two irreconcilable failure policies.
findings.evidence: constraints ("When QA is skipped"): "When the `sycophancy-correction`/artifact-refiner binary is absent, the gate logs the skip and passes (graceful degradation)"; SKILL.md line 36: "An unavailable or unresolved review blocks certification, not implementation."
findings.suggested_fix: Align the skill's unavailability policy with the constraint (skip-and-log with a recorded skip), or explicitly state which contexts block and which degrade.

findings.claim: The packet's parsed frontmatter shows the description collapsed to the literal folded-scalar marker ">" and tags hoisted out of metadata, so any consumer parsing the frontmatter the same way sees an empty trigger description and no tags.
findings.evidence: frontmatter field: `"description": ">"`, `"metadata": {}`, `"tags": "[process, orchestration, recovery]"` as a top-level string, versus the nested `metadata: tags:` structure in SKILL.md lines 4-8.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single-line (or double-quoted) description string and verify metadata nesting survives the actual loader's parser; confirm the real runtime parses the folded scalar correctly.

findings.claim: "One regeneration is allowed" has no defined object — regeneration of the review, of the projections, or of the receipts — making the instruction unactionable and its limit unenforceable.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md line 34: "One regeneration is allowed when the screening score is at least `0.4` or reports a high/critical pattern." No prior sentence establishes anything labeled a "regeneration".
findings.suggested_fix: Name the artifact being regenerated and the command that performs it (e.g. "re-run `repair` once").

findings.claim: The agent is told to "use the exact progress signal returned by the command" but the output schema of `status`/`evaluate` (field names, the `blocked` encoding) is documented nowhere in the packet.
findings.evidence: SKILL.md line 24-25: "Treat `blocked` as a real lifecycle blocker and use the exact progress signal returned by the command." references/receipt-contract.md is scoped to receipts, not command output, and no example output is shown.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short example of `status`/`evaluate` output, or point to the contract section that defines the progress-signal fields.
